short: A German battlecruiser whose flight to Constantinople in 1914 was instrumental in bringing the Ottoman Empire into the First World War.
full:
Commissioned on 2 July 1912, SMS Goeben was a Moltke-class battlecruiser assigned to the Imperial German Navy's Mediterranean Division. When war erupted in August 1914, she was pursued by the British Mediterranean Fleet but successfully evaded them alongside her escort, the light cruiser SMS Breslau, and escaped through the Dardanelles into Constantinople.

Her arrival had immense strategic consequences. She was formally transferred to the Ottoman Navy and renamed Yavuz Sultan Selim, though she remained under German command. In October 1914, she bombarded Russian Black Sea ports, effectively forcing the Ottoman Empire to enter the war on the side of the Central Powers. She outlasted the conflict to serve as the flagship of the new Turkish Republic, remaining in active service until 1950.
